title: An employee can approve their own leave request
summary: The approve endpoint does not check who is calling. Any logged-in employee can approve their own request, or a colleague's. The page hides the Approve button, but the server accepts the call, so managers lose control over who is off.
steps: Request one day of leave. It appears as pending.
Send POST /api/requests/<id>/approve with Ben's session (the browser console is enough).
Reload: the request is approved, decided by Ben himself.

expected.text: Only a manager can approve, and nobody can decide their own request. Anyone else gets HTTP 403 and the request stays pending.

actual: HTTP 200. The request is stored as approved with decided_by = Ben's own user id.

how.state: SELECT status, decided_by FROM requests WHERE id = 1 → approved, 2 (Ben)
how.byDesignCheck: PRD R4 is explicit, and rejectRequest already enforces both checks.

hint: In approveRequest, do what rejectRequest already does: 403 unless user.role is 'manager', and 403 when req.user_id === user.id. Check both before the UPDATE.
